script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Good morning, Riverside Sports Centre. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Hi, I'd like to join the swimming club for adults, please.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Certainly. Can I take your name?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: It's Daniel Marsh. That's M-A-R-S-H.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Thank you, Mr Marsh. And a contact number?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Lovely. We run adult sessions on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at seven, and also on Saturday mornings at nine.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Saturday would suit me best. Is there a beginners' group?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Yes, but it's on Sundays at ten. The Saturday session is for improvers.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: I can swim a little, so I'll try Saturday then.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Membership is forty-five pounds a month, or four hundred and ten pounds if you pay for the whole year.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: I'll start with the monthly option. Do I need to bring anything?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Just a towel and a swimming cap. Locker keys cost a pound, which you get back.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Great. And where do I park?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: There's a car park behind the library, opposite the main entrance. It's free for members.

questions.why: Sayıları rakam rakam yaz; boşluk farkı sorun değil.
'Saturday would suit me best … I'll try Saturday then'.
'forty-five pounds a month'. Yıllık ücret (410) çeldirici.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Welcome to the Harbour Heritage Walk. Before we start, a few practical points. The walk lasts about ninety minutes, and we'll finish at the old customs house, where there is a café.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: The first stop is the lighthouse, built in 1857, which is the oldest building on this part of the coast. Please don't climb the stairs, as they are closed for repairs until next spring.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: After that we'll walk along the fish market, which operates every morning except Monday. If you'd like to buy something, I recommend the smoked salmon, which is a local speciality.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Then we reach the maritime museum. It's free on the first Sunday of each month, but today there is a small entrance fee of six pounds. Photography is allowed everywhere except in the model ship gallery.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Finally, a safety note: the path by the harbour wall can be slippery when it's wet, so please wear suitable shoes.

questions.q: How long does the walk last?
Why can't visitors climb the lighthouse stairs?
options: They are too dangerous in strong wind.
They are open to staff only.

questions.q: On which day is the fish market closed?

questions.why: 'a small entrance fee of six pounds'. 'Free on the first Sunday' çeldirici.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: So, Maya, Tom, how's your project on renewable energy going?

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: We've decided to focus on wind power, but Tom thinks we should include solar too.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: I just think a comparison would be more interesting. Wind farms are cheaper to run, but solar panels can be installed on any roof.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: That's a fair point, but remember the word limit is three thousand words. Covering both might make the report rather superficial.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: That's what worries me. What if we look at wind in depth and just mention solar in the conclusion?

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: That could work. What about your sources?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: We found a government report from 2019, but it's rather old.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Then look for something more recent. The university library has a database with industry statistics up to last year. And do interview someone if you can; it'll strengthen your methodology section.

script.speaker: Maya
script.text: We could email the engineer who gave the guest lecture.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Excellent idea. When is your draft due?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Friday the fourteenth.

script.speaker: Tutor
script.text: Send it to me by Wednesday so I can give you feedback first.

questions.q: What does Tom want to include in the project?
options: Solar power as well as wind
questions.why: 'Tom thinks we should include solar too'.

questions.q: What is the tutor's concern about covering both?
options: There would not be enough sources.
It would be too long for the deadline.

questions.q: What is the problem with the government report?
questions.why: 'a government report from 2019, but it's rather old'.

options: The engineer from the guest lecture
questions.why: 'email the engineer who gave the guest lecture'.

questions.q: They should send the draft to the tutor by ______ (ONE WORD)
questions.why: Teslim tarihi Cuma (14'ü), ama tutor'a 'by Wednesday' göndermeleri isteniyor.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Today I'd like to talk about octopus intelligence. Octopuses have around five hundred million neurons, roughly the same number as a dog, but unlike mammals, about two-thirds of these neurons are located in their arms rather than in the central brain. This means each arm can, to some extent, make its own decisions.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Researchers first became interested in octopus behaviour in laboratories, where animals learned to open jars to reach food. Later field studies showed that octopuses use tools in the wild: some carry coconut shells and assemble them as portable shelters.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Another remarkable ability is camouflage. Octopuses change both colour and skin texture within a fraction of a second, even though scientists believe they are colour-blind. One theory is that their skin contains light-sensitive proteins.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: However, octopuses live only one to two years, which limits what they can learn from others, since most never meet their parents. This short life span is one reason why scientists consider their intelligence so puzzling.

questions.q: About two-thirds of the neurons are in their ______ (ONE WORD)
questions.why: 'located in their arms rather than in the central brain'.

questions.q: In laboratories, octopuses learned to open ______ to reach food. (ONE WORD)
questions.why: 'learned to open jars to reach food'.

questions.q: In the wild, some carry coconut ______ and use them as shelters. (ONE WORD)

questions.why: 'even though scientists believe they are colour-blind'.

questions.q: Why does the lecturer find octopus intelligence puzzling?
options: They live a short time and rarely learn from parents.
They cannot be studied in laboratories.
questions.why: Son bölüm: kısa ömür + ebeveynle tanışmama.
